Absent on a home where natives were not built — skipped, not an error.

retainedAgainstIntuition.basis: ALL processor modules retained (28,682,724 B total). Ghidra enumerates every processor's language metadata at startup; only the target language's compiled .sla actually loads (x86-64.sla in the traced run). Armor analyzes arbitrary files across architectures and formats; dropping processors would silently narrow coverage for 3% of the home.

RETAINED BY EVIDENCE: the Function ID analyzer opened all ten Visual Studio .fidbf databases (204,171,136 B) during the traced run. They are data, not Mach-O, so they never blocked notarization. Cutting them would change PE analysis (library-function identification) — a product decision, not a prune-by-evidence.

RETAINED: the run opened the generic C-library data-type archive and symbol/string data; PE and Mach-O targets use the win32/mac_10.9 typeinfo and symbols subtrees of the same directory. Armor analyzes arbitrary files, so the whole data tree stays.
